# On which topics am I absent while a competitor holds the ground?

> Tag prompts by topic, read the topic map (held, contested, to win back, blind spot) and choose where to put the effort, one topic at a time.

[← Documentation contents](../README.md) · [Lire cette page en français](../../fr/cas-usage/themes-ou-je-suis-absent.md)

Facturo’s prompts cover several subjects: quotes, chasing unpaid invoices, e-invoicing, for example. Reading visibility prompt by prompt does not tell you where the real gap is. Grouped by topic, the prompts show the subjects where a competitor is settled and those nobody holds yet.

<a id="what-you-need"></a>

## What you need

- Tagged prompts: a topic and an intent for each. A small model sets them for less than a cent; you can also set them yourself, for free.
- Enough answers read per topic: below 5, the topic’s status is “too early to tell”.

<a id="steps"></a>

## Steps

1. **Tag the prompts.** On **Prompts**, the banner offers **Tag the prompts** with its price. Each prompt gets a topic and an intent (learn, compare, buy). After this first click, added prompts are tagged automatically; you can turn that off in the same place. A tag is corrected on the prompt page with **Edit tags**; a tag set by hand is no longer changed by the model.

2. **Read the topic map.** Further down **Prompts**, the **Topic map** gives for each topic the number of prompts, Facturo’s presence (answers where it appears, out of answers received), the **Most mentioned brand** and a **Status**.

   ![Read the topic map](../../../public/docs/captures/en/questions.webp)

3. **Understand the statuses.** **Held**: Facturo is in 6 answers out of 10 or more, and no other brand is mentioned more often. **Contested**: present, but less often, or overtaken. **To win back**: absent while another brand is mentioned in 3 answers out of 10 or more. **Blind spot**: absent, and nobody reaches 3 answers out of 10. The rule for each status is repeated in the column’s help bubble.

4. **Go down to the prompts.** Clicking a topic filters the prompts table to that topic. **Group by** **Topic** sorts the whole table by topic. On each prompt, the **On this prompt** block tells you **Who wins** and which pages make them win.

5. **Move on to actions.** On a prompt page, **Related actions** leads to the work list rows that follow from it: pages to appear on, pages to rewrite, videos to make.

<a id="decision"></a>

## The decision it supports

- **To win back**: a competitor holds the topic. The work starts from the pages that get it cited.
- **Blind spot**: nobody holds the topic. A good page may be enough to get in first.
- **Contested**: you are already there. Strengthening what works often costs less than conquering a topic.
- **Held**: keep watching, without spending the week on it.

> [!WARNING]
> **Before you act**
>
> With one or two runs per prompt, a topic’s status is a snapshot, not a trend. The map counts interface readings only, deep measurements excluded; Facturo’s share is counted on all answers received, other brands’ on answers whose brands have been read. A badly tagged topic skews its row: review the model’s tags.
